title: URL Shortener
summary: A managed redirect service. The slug is a stable identifier that routes every click through our system once, so the redirect can be measured and controlled — which is why analytics sits off the critical path.

nodes.label: Click
nodes.notes: Someone follows ourdomain.com/aB7kQ2 from SMS, a post, or a QR code. This request is latency-critical: the user is staring at a blank tab until it resolves.

nodes.label: Admin / API caller
nodes.notes: Marketers, product teams, and internal services creating and managing links. Low volume, high privilege — the opposite profile to the redirect path.

nodes.label: CDN
nodes.notes: Terminates TLS at the edge and absorbs repeat traffic on hot slugs. A cached 301 never reaches our origin at all — the cheapest redirect is the one we don't serve.

nodes.label: Load balancer
nodes.notes: Spreads origin traffic across redirect service instances and sheds load when a region degrades.

nodes.label: Redirect Service
nodes.notes: The critical path, and deliberately the dumbest service here: resolve slug, check status and expiry, emit one event, return 301/302. Anything else belongs off this path.

nodes.label: Link Service
nodes.notes: Create, update, disable, and expire links. Writes are rare relative to reads, so this scales independently from the redirect path.

nodes.label: Key Generation
nodes.notes: Hands out unique slugs from a pre-allocated range so link creation never needs a collision-retry loop against the database.

nodes.label: Redirect Cache
nodes.notes: Slug → destination, with a TTL. Lazy expiry on read plus active sampling in the background. The hit rate here is what keeps the database small enough to be boring.

nodes.label: Link Store
nodes.notes: Source of truth for the redirect object: destination, owner, campaign, status, expiry. Keyed by slug, so reads are a single partition lookup — no scan, no join.

nodes.label: Click Event Queue
nodes.notes: The seam that keeps redirect latency independent of analytics latency. Start with a durable queue and a dead-letter queue; move to Kafka only when raw click history needs broad replay.

nodes.label: Analytics Workers
nodes.notes: Enrich click events with referrer, coarse geography, and device, then aggregate. Scales on queue depth, entirely separately from the redirect fleet.

nodes.label: Analytics Store
nodes.notes: Clicks over time by campaign, referrer, geography, device. Read by dashboards, never by the redirect path.

edges.label: GET /aB7kQ2
edges.notes: The whole product, from the user's point of view: one GET that should end in a redirect within a few tens of milliseconds.

edges.label: cache miss
edges.notes: Only misses reach the origin. Cacheability is a design decision: 301s cache hard, 302s let us change the destination later.

edges.label: GET slug
edges.notes: First stop on every resolve. A hit here ends the lookup.

edges.label: cache miss
edges.notes: Read-through on a miss, then populate the cache with a TTL.

edges.label: click event
edges.notes: Fire-and-forget. If this publish fails we still serve the redirect — losing a click event is cheaper than adding latency to every click.

edges.label: invalidate
edges.notes: Destination changes have to invalidate, or a stale cache keeps sending traffic to the old target long after the campaign moved.

flows.label: Resolve a link (cache hit)
flows.notes: The path that has to be fast
steps: Someone follows a short link. The clock starts here.
TLS terminates at the edge; the CDN checks for a cached redirect.
Miss at the edge, so the request goes to the origin load balancer.
Routed to any redirect instance — they hold no session state.
Redis answers slug → destination in about 2ms. Return 301 and we're done.

flows.label: Resolve a link (cold slug)
flows.notes: What a cache miss actually costs
steps: A click on a slug nobody has touched recently.
Edge miss — nothing cached for this one.
Origin load balancer picks an instance.
Cache miss too. This is the expensive case, and the one to design for.
Single-partition read by slug: destination, status, expiry.
The redirect is answered, several milliseconds slower than a hit.
Populate the cache with a TTL so the next click takes the fast path.

flows.label: Record a click
steps: The redirect service publishes one small event and returns immediately.
The queue absorbs the burst and retries failures into a dead-letter queue.
Workers enrich with referrer, geography, and device, then aggregate.
Results land where dashboards read them — seconds behind, which is fine.

flows.label: Create a short link
steps: An authenticated caller posts a destination URL and campaign metadata.
Through the same load balancer, but a completely different traffic profile.
The link service handles it — scaled separately from the redirect fleet.
Key generation hands back a unique slug from a pre-allocated range.
No collision retry loop was needed, so the write can proceed directly.
The redirect object is written as the new source of truth.
